title: Assembling Cooled LED Illuminator
author: Jakub Nedbal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcrniv5e

steps.title: Prepare LED strips and heatsink
steps.instruction: Cut a 2‑meter self‑adhesive LED strip into ten 200 mm (8 in) segments along the solder‑pad lines, then draw nine equally spaced guide lines on a 200 mm × 150 mm × 40 mm heatsink (thermal resistance 0.5 °C/K) using a permanent marker and ruler; the first line starts 15.5 mm from the edge and lines are spaced 15.5 mm apart (calculated from Nₛ=10, wₛ=10 mm, N_G=9, w_G≈5.5 mm, w_L≈15.5 mm). Peel the backing from each LED segment and attach them one‑by‑one to the heatsink along the drawn lines, keeping all segments oriented identically.

steps.title: Solder LED strips together
steps.instruction: Cut red and black 0.5 mm² wire into nine 30 mm (1 in) pieces, strip insulation from both ends of each piece, then solder the red wires to the anode (+) pads and the black wires to the cathode (–) pads of adjacent LED segments. If the soldering iron cannot heat the pads while the strips are on the heatsink, briefly lift the strip ends, solder, and reseat the adhesive backing.

steps.title: Attach axial fans to heatsink
steps.instruction: Apply a liberal amount of general‑purpose solvent‑based glue to the side of the heatsink and press each of the four axial fans (frame against the heatsink, rotor/blades facing outward, power leads pointing toward the LED side) onto the glue, spacing them side‑by‑side. Dab glue on each fan’s power‑lead area, press the leads into the glue, and secure temporarily with electricians tape; repeat for all fans. Reinforce any LED‑strip edges that tend to peel by dispensing glue along the strip edges, pressing the strips flat, and weighting lifted sections with a 1 in stainless‑steel post (or similar) while the glue cures. Allow the glue to dry (typically ≥1 hour, depending on glue and environment).

steps.title: Mount LED controller on heatsink
steps.instruction: Place the heatsink on its side on a table edge, apply general‑purpose solvent‑based glue to the side where the LED controller will sit, and press the controller onto the glue ensuring at least 6 mm (¼ in) clearance between the bottom of the heatsink and the bottom of the controller (to clear the orbital shaker rim). Let the glue set for 10–30 minutes. Then solder short red and black 0.5 mm² wires to an unconnected end of the LED strip (red to (+) pad, black to (–) pad) and solder the power‑supply leads to the first LED strip (red to anode, black to cathode). Trim each fan’s power leads to a length that comfortably reaches the LED controller’s screw terminals, strip the ends, and connect each fan’s red and black leads to a neighboring pair of terminals on the controller (red to (+) terminal, black to (–) terminal). Connect the LED‑strip leads to the controller terminal labeled “LED”.

steps.title: Test LED controller operation
steps.instruction: Connect a 30 V/1 A power supply to the LED controller and plug it into a socket. Toggle the switch through the three positions: OFF (LEDs and fans off), TRICKLE (LEDs dim, fans stationary), and CONTROL (LEDs bright, fans spinning). Adjust LED brightness with the rotary switch from maximum (•) to minimum (6) as needed.

description: Summary This protocol explained the procedure of mounting LED strips to a heatsink, adding axial fans for cooling, and the LED controller. It described the electrical connection of these parts and finally shown how to verify the function of the cooled LED illuminator. The next document will describe how to cut a clear acrylic sheet for the illuminated orbital shaker.
